column3: “Stealthily introduce” is rendered “secretly introduce,” and “imminent” “swift.”
NASB follows the critical text (“sensuality”); “denigrated” is rendered “maligned.”
“Covetousness” is rendered “greed,” and “fabricated” “false.”
NASB follows the critical text (“pits of darkness”); “delivered to Tartarus” is rendered “cast them into hell.”
“One of eight” is rendered “with seven others,” and “herald” “preacher.”
NASB follows the critical text (“those who would live ungodly”); NASB adds “if.”
“Distressed” is rendered “oppressed,” and “lawless” “unprincipled men”; NASB adds “if.”
NASB adds parentheses.
“Devout” is rendered “godly”; NASB supplies “how to.”
“Glorious ones” is rendered “angelic majesties”; “walking after the flesh in the passion of defilement” is rendered “indulge the flesh in its corrupt desires.”
NASB follows the critical text (“before the Lord”).
NASB follows the critical text (“born,” “be destroyed”); NASB supplies “those creatures.”
NASB follows the critical text (“suffering wrong”); “carousal in daytime” is rendered “revel in the daytime,” and “feasting with you” “as they carouse with you.”
NASB follows the critical text (“greed”); “children of a curse” is rendered “accursed children.”
NASB has “Beor”; the Greek has “Bosor.”
NASB supplies “for.”
NASB follows the critical text (“and mists,” without “forever”); “gloom of darkness” is rendered “black darkness.”
NASB follows the critical text (“barely escape”).
“Subdued” is rendered “overcome.”
NASB has “the Lord and Savior” without “our,” which matches the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “our.”
NASB follows the critical text (“to turn away”).
NASB supplies “returns” in the second proverb.
